mainTopic: How far צירוף and other טומאה rules for קודש reach: a כלי joining its contents, the fourth level of impurity, and one hand making the other impure.
overview: On the previous page, רבי חנין brought a פסוק to show that a כלי joins everything inside it into one unit for קודש. רב כהנא asked why רבי עקיבא then needed to testify about this. The גמרא answers that the testimony covers only rabbinic extensions: שירי מנחה, which no longer need a כלי, and קטורת or לבונה piled on a flat board with no 'inside'. It then notes that רבי יוחנן disagrees with רבי חנין, because he holds that our משנה rests on רבי עקיבא's testimony. Next, a ברייתא of רבי יוסי teaches that a third level of impurity for קודש comes from the Torah and a fourth level comes from a קל וחומר. The גמרא shows the Torah source for the third level in a פסוק in ויקרא. Then רב שיזבי limits the משנה's rule that one impure hand makes the other impure for קודש to a case where the hands are in contact with the קודש. אביי challenges him from a ברייתא about a dry hand. Finally ריש לקיש begins to limit the rule to a person's own hand, and his statement continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The testimony is needed for leftover meal-offering flour
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers רב כהנא: רבי עקיבא's testimony is needed only for שירי מנחה, which no longer need a כלי. By Torah law a כלי joins only things that need a כלי, but רבנן decreed that it joins even things that do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The testimony is needed only for the leftovers of a מנחה. By Torah law, if something needs a כלי, the כלי joins it into one unit. If it does not need a כלי, the כלי does not join it. Then רבנן came and decreed that even if it does not need a כלי, the כלי still joins it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי חנין's Torah source by showing that רבי עקיבא's testimony is about a different case, one that is only rabbinic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah rule of צירוף applies only to items that need a כלי to become holy. Once the קומץ has been offered, the leftover flour (שירי מנחה) no longer needs a כלי, so it is not joined by Torah law. רבי עקיבא's testimony teaches the extra rabbinic decree that joins even these leftovers.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for… (limits a teaching to a specific case)
The leftover flour of a meal-offering, eaten by the כהנים after the קומץ is offered
By Torah law
Joins together into one unit (for טומאה)
They (the Sages) decreed

steps.confusionAlert: This answer does not say that צירוף is only rabbinic. The basic rule is still Torah law; only the extension to things that do not need a כלי is rabbinic.
steps.whyThisMatters: This splits the rule into two layers: a Torah core (items that need a כלי) and a rabbinic extension. The rest of the סוגיא builds on that split.

phrases.english: It is needed only for the remainders of a meal-offering.
phrases.notes: 'It' is רבי עקיבא's testimony, which רב כהנא asked about on the previous page.

phrases.english: For by Torah law, something that requires a vessel —
the vessel combines it;
something that does not require a vessel —
the vessel does not combine it.
And the Sages came and decreed

phrases.aramaic: דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּאֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לִכְלִי —
phrases.english: that even though it does not require a vessel,
the vessel combines it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב כהנא's challenge (on the previous page) against רבי חנין's Torah source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the case (אוקימתא): the testimony refers to a case that is only rabbinic.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא's testimony seemed to teach the basic rule of צירוף, which would make רבי חנין's פסוק unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: The testimony teaches the rabbinic extension to שירי מנחה, which do not need a כלי.

steps.title: But what about incense and frankincense?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer: it works for סולת, but קטורת and לבונה do need a כלי, so why are they in רבי עקיבא's list?
steps.simpleTranslation: That works for the flour. But what can you say about the קטורת and the לבונה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave by pointing to the other items in רבי עקיבא's list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שירי מנחה answer explains only the סולת. קטורת and לבונה still need a כלי, so they are joined by Torah law, and there seems to be no reason for רבי עקיבא to testify about them.

keyTerms.meaning: It works out well (for this part)
Fine flour
Incense
Frankincense
What is there to say? (a challenge)

phrases.english: It works out well for flour;
but with regard to incense and frankincense, what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּינַח סֹלֶת, קְטוֹרֶת וּלְבוֹנָה מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in Step 1 as only partly covering רבי עקיבא's list.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 1's claim that the testimony is only about rabbinic cases like שירי מנחה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קטורת and לבונה always need a כלי, so they are joined by Torah law, and the testimony about them would be unnecessary.

steps.title: Piled on a flat leather board
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה answers: the case is where the קטורת and לבונה were piled on a flat board (קרטבלא). By Torah law only a כלי with an 'inside' joins its contents, but רבנן enacted that even a flat one joins them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: for example, where he piled them on a flat leather board. By Torah law, a כלי that has an inside joins its contents, and one without an inside does not. Then רבנן came and enacted that even if it has no inside, it joins them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by finding a rabbinic case for קטורת and לבונה too: a flat board with no hollow inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds a second limit on the Torah rule: the כלי must have a תוך, a hollow inside that holds things. A flat board does not count by Torah law, so joining items on it is rabbinic. That is what רבי עקיבא's testimony about קטורת and לבונה teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: He piled them up
A flat leather board or tray
It has an inside (a hollow that holds things)
They enacted

steps.whatToRemember: By Torah law a כלי joins its contents only if (1) the items need a כלי and (2) the כלי has an inside. רבנן extended צירוף to both missing cases, and רבי עקיבא's testimony teaches those extensions.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said that Rabba bar Avuh said:
For example, where he piled them up on a leather board.
For by Torah law, one that has an inside combines;
one that does not have an inside does not combine.
And the Sages came and enacted

phrases.aramaic: דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּאֵין לוֹ תּוֹךְ — מְצָרֵף.
phrases.english: that even though it does not have an inside, it combines.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 2 by limiting the case to a flat board.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the case (אוקימתא) to a כלי without an inside.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: קטורת and לבונה in any כלי are joined by Torah law, so testifying about them would be pointless.
steps.terutzMaskana: The testimony refers to items on a flat board, which are joined only by rabbinic enactment.

steps.title: רבי חנין disagrees with רבי יוחנן's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רבי חנין's view (that צירוף comes from the Torah) disagrees with רבי חייא בר אבא, who quoted רבי יוחנן that our משנה was taught based on רבי עקיבא's testimony.
steps.simpleTranslation: This view of רבי חנין disagrees with רבי חייא בר אבא. For רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: this משנה was taught based on the testimony of רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps back and points out that another אמורא understands our משנה differently from רבי חנין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן says our משנה's rule that a כלי joins its contents comes from רבי עקיבא's testimony. That makes it a rabbinic rule. This conflicts with רבי חנין, who found a Torah source in a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: And it disagrees with
His testimony
Was taught (said of a משנה)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two approaches to צירוף בכלי: רבי חנין says it is Torah law (from a פסוק), while רבי יוחנן says our משנה rests on רבי עקיבא's testimony and is rabbinic.

phrases.aramaic: וּפְלִיגָא דְּרַבִּי חָנִין אַדְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא.
phrases.english: And Rabbi Ḥanin's view disagrees with that of Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: For Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:

phrases.aramaic: מֵעֵדוּתוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא נִשְׁנֵית מִשְׁנָה זוֹ.
phrases.english: This mishna was taught based on Rabbi Akiva's testimony.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּפְלִיגָא דְּרַבִּי חָנִין אַדְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רבי חנין, the גמרא notes that רבי יוחנן's approach disagrees with him.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוחנן, our משנה's rule that a כלי joins its contents comes from רבי עקיבא's testimony and is rabbinic.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's proof that a fourth level of impurity applies to sacred food
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that רביעי בקודש is פסול. It brings a ברייתא where רבי יוסי proves this with a קל וחומר from a מחוסר כיפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said a fourth level of impurity disqualifies sacred food. A ברייתא teaches: רבי יוסי said, how do we know this? By logic. A person who still owes his atonement offering may eat תרומה, yet he may not eat קודש. A שלישי already counts as disqualified when it is תרומה, so surely it should create a fourth level for קודש. So the third level for קודש comes from the Torah, and the fourth comes from a קל וחומר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and brings a ברייתא that gives its source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר works like this. A מחוסר כיפורים is not a problem for תרומה, but he is a problem for קודש, so קודש is stricter. A שלישי already counts as disqualified for תרומה, so for the stricter קודש it should go one step further and make a רביעי.

keyTerms.meaning: Fourth level of impurity, one more step removed from the original source
Third level of impurity
Someone who has already immersed but has not yet brought the offering that finishes his purification
An argument from a lighter case to a stricter case
'It is logical', the opening words of a reasoned proof

phrases.english: The fourth degree with sacred food is disqualified.
It is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Yosei said:
From where do we know that a fourth degree with sacred food is disqualified?
It is a matter of logic:
Now, if one who is lacking atonement,
who is permitted to eat terumah,
is disqualified from sacred food,
then a third degree, which is disqualified in terumah,
is it not logical that it should make a fourth degree for sacred food?
So we have learned the third degree for sacred food from the Torah,
and the fourth degree by a kal vachomer.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: מִנַּיִן לָרְבִיעִי בַּקֹּדֶשׁ שֶׁהוּא פָּסוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the צירוף discussion and starts on the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fourth level of impurity disqualifies קודש. The third level comes from the Torah and the fourth comes from a קל וחומר.

steps.title: Where does the Torah teach the third level for sacred food?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the Torah source of the ברייתא's claim that שלישי לקודש is מן התורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said the third level for קודש comes from the Torah. From where?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about one claim in the ברייתא. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי's קל וחומר rests on the third level being a Torah rule. So the גמרא wants to see the actual פסוק behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: A rule that comes from the Torah itself

phrases.english: The third degree for sacred food from the Torah, from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of one claim made in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches the third level of impurity for קודש.

steps.title: The verse about meat that touches anything impure
steps.stepSummary: The answer is the פסוק 'והבשר אשר יגע בכל טמא לא יאכל'. 'Any impure thing' includes a שני, so meat that touches a שני becomes a שלישי and may not be eaten. The fourth level comes from the קל וחומר already given.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And the meat that touches any impure thing shall not be eaten.' This includes meat that touched a שני, and still the Torah says it may not be eaten. That makes it a שלישי. The fourth level comes from the קל וחומר we just said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by pointing to a פסוק about sacred meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'כל' (any) is read broadly, so it covers even something that is only a שני. Meat that touches a שני becomes a שלישי, and the Torah forbids it. So the Torah itself counts a third level for קודש.

keyTerms.meaning: Second level of impurity
'The Merciful One', a way of referring to the Torah
'We are dealing with'

phrases.english: As it is written: "And the meat that touches
any impure thing shall not be eaten."
Are we not dealing even with where it touched a second degree?
phrases.notes: Since the פסוק says 'any', it covers even touching a שני, which makes the meat a שלישי.

phrases.english: And the Merciful One says, "It shall not be eaten."
The fourth degree from a kal vachomer:
that is what we said.
phrases.notes: This points back to רבי יוסי's קל וחומר in the ברייתא.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: וְהַבָּשָׂר אֲשֶׁר יִגַּע בְּכׇל טָמֵא לֹא יֵאָכֵל
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'בכל טמא' includes a שני, so a שלישי of קודש is forbidden by the Torah. The fourth level comes from רבי יוסי's קל וחומר.
steps.whatToRemember: For קודש: the third level comes from the Torah (ויקרא 7:19), and the fourth comes from a קל וחומר based on מחוסר כיפורים.

steps.title: רב שיזבי: one hand makes the other impure only when in contact
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about an impure hand. It says that for תרומה the other hand stays pure, but for קודש both become impure. רב שיזבי limits the קודש rule to a case of חיבורין, where the hands are in contact with the קודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And for תרומה, if one hand became impure, and so on.' רב שיזבי said: the rule that for קודש one hand makes the other impure was taught only when they are joined together with the קודש. If they are not joined, then no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, and רב שיזבי narrows when the stricter rule for קודש applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is strict for קודש, where one impure hand makes the other impure too. רב שיזבי says this strictness applies only when the pure hand is in contact with the קודש at the same time. Otherwise the other hand is not affected.

keyTerms.meaning: Being joined or in contact, here meaning together with the sacred food
'Etc.', which shows the משנה is quoted only in part

phrases.english: "And with terumah, if one became impure, etc."
phrases.notes: The משנה says that for תרומה the other hand stays pure, but for קודש both hands become impure.

phrases.english: Rav Sheizevi said: They taught this when they are in contact,
phrases.notes: He is talking about the strict rule for קודש, where one hand makes the other impure.

phrases.english: but when not in contact, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new line of the משנה about hands.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For קודש, one impure hand makes the other impure only when they are in contact with the קודש.

steps.title: אביי's challenge from a ברייתא about a dry hand
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב שיזבי with a ברייתא. In it, רבי says a dry impure hand makes the other hand able to make קודש impure, though not תרומה. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says the other hand only disqualifies the קודש and does not make it impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי objected: a dry hand makes the other hand impure, so that it makes קודש impure, but not תרומה. These are the words of רבי. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: it only disqualifies, but it does not make impure.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי starts a challenge by quoting a ברייתא. The ברייתא seems to say one hand makes the other impure for קודש without mentioning contact. The next step (step 10) spells out exactly how this contradicts רב שיזבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא stresses that even a dry impure hand makes the other hand impure for קודש. The next step explains why that stress clashes with רב שיזבי's limit. The two תנאים in the ברייתא disagree only about how strong the second hand's impurity is: whether it makes the קודש impure, or only disqualifies it as a רביעי.

keyTerms.meaning: A dry hand
Its fellow, meaning the other hand
To disqualify, making the food unfit without passing impurity further

steps.confusionAlert: 'לפסול' and 'לטמא' are not the same thing. 'לטמא' means the food becomes impure and can pass impurity on. 'לפסול' means the food is only unfit and passes impurity no further.

phrases.english: Abaye raised an objection to him:
A dry hand makes its fellow hand impure
so that it renders sacred food impure,
but not terumah. These are the words of Rebbi.
Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda says:
to disqualify, but not to render impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב שיזבי's limit from step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב שיזבי's claim that one hand makes the other impure for קודש only when they are in contact.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא stresses that even a dry hand makes the other hand impure for קודש. That stress is a real חידוש only if the rule applies even without חיבורין, as step 10 spells out.

steps.title: Why the dry-hand case is a problem for רב שיזבי
steps.stepSummary: אביי shows that the ברייתא's point about a dry hand only makes sense if the rule applies even without contact. That goes against רב שיזבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense if you say the rule applies even when the hands are not touching the קודש. Then that is the big new point of mentioning a dry hand. But if you say the rule applies only when the hands touch the קודש, and not otherwise, then what big new point does the dry hand teach?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי is finishing his challenge from step 9. He explains exactly why the ברייתא about a dry hand contradicts רב שיזבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A dry hand normally would not pass impurity to the other hand, so saying even a dry hand does it is a big חידוש. That חידוש fits a rule that applies even without contact. If the rule applies only with חיבורין, where the worry is direct touching, mentioning a dry hand adds nothing special. So the ברייתא seems to argue against רב שיזבי's limit.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted (opens the side that works well)
The big new point, the חידוש of a case
Dry (a dry hand)
In contact, where the hands are touching the קודש
Yes / no

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether a dry hand counts. It is why the ברייתא bothered to stress a dry hand. That stress only makes sense if the rule works even without contact.

phrases.english: It makes sense if you say the rule applies even when not in contact:
that is the big new point of the dry hand.
phrases.notes: This refers to רבי's words in the ברייתא from step 9: even a dry impure hand affects the other hand.

phrases.english: But if you say: when in contact, yes, the rule applies,
but when not in contact, no, it does not,
then what is the big new point of the dry hand?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the reasoning behind the ברייתא that אביי brought in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב שיזבי's claim (step 8) that the קודש rule applies only בחיבורין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא stresses a dry hand as a חידוש. That stress only matters if the rule applies even without contact. Limiting it to חיבורין makes the dry-hand detail pointless.

steps.title: ריש לקיש limits the rule to one's own hand
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a related amoraic statement. ריש לקיש says the rule that one hand makes the other impure was taught only about a person's own hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: ריש לקיש said: They taught this only about his own hand,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts quoting a statement of ריש לקיש on the same topic. His sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far the topic was whether the rule needs contact with the קודש. ריש לקיש adds a different kind of limit: whose hand is being made impure. The rule applies only when the second hand belongs to the same person.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated (brings a related teaching of the אמוראים)
They taught this only in the case of (a limiting formula)

phrases.english: It was also stated: ריש לקיש said:
They taught this only about his own hand,
phrases.notes: He means the second hand that becomes impure must belong to the same person. His sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the debate over the contact limit, the גמרא brings an amoraic statement that limits the same rule from the משנה in a different way.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ריש לקיש: the rule that one impure hand makes the other hand impure for קודש was taught only about the person's own hand.
